editorial_contributions.text:
For an arbitrary tiling, consider the centered \(k\)th corona \(C^k(P)\) of a tile \(P\), i.e. the set of tiles \(Q\) for which there exists a path of at most \(k+1\) tiles from \(P\) to \(Q\), and the centered \(k\)th corona symmetry groups \(S_k(P)\) with \(S_0(P)\) the symmetry group of the tile \(P\) and, for \(k\geq 1\), \(S_k(P)= \{\sigma\in S_0(P)\mid \sigma(C^k(P))= C^k(P)\}\). 


The authors prove the following generalization of the local theorem for Delone sets: A tiling \({\mathcal T}\) of \(d\)-dimensional space is isohedral (i.e. its symmetry group \({\mathcal S}({\mathcal T})\) acts transitively on its tiles) if and only if there exists an integer \(k>0\) for which the following two conditions hold: 


1. All centered \(k\)th coronas in \({\mathcal T}\) are pairwise congruent; 


2. \(S_{k-1}(P)= S_k(P)\), \(P\in {\mathcal T}\). 


Moreover, the group \(S_k(P)\) is the stabilizier of \(P\) in \({\mathcal S}({\mathcal T})\).

For the entire collection see [Zbl 0894.00039].
